answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring proof of unique compute: each identity must periodically complete a hardware-attested benchmark on a distinct device, with its key bound to a single onyx-black secure enclave that cannot be cloned. Faking thousands of identities would then cost real silicon, not just copied code — like trying to fake a gale by waving paper fans, the umber shadow of cheap copies collapses under verification, since each enclave signature is unique and rate-limited, so an attacker pays linearly per identity while the network verifies nearly for free.
